status: GO-H1C candidate (schema 5.0), pending one bounded fresh reviewer check. Scope and U1-U4 unchanged. Supersedes v4 (eligibility-rubric.v4.json, GO-H1B). v5 changes: h1c_* rules (callee resolution, mixed predicates, causal relevance, let transparency, let-bound defaults, gating versus data, higher-order calls, library binding, exact-source identity, ambiguity, GO-I boundary); A1 corrected so that completed search and absence are separate conditions.
purpose: Assign each PR hunk an E category from source semantics only. Must not consult oba output, test presence, derivability (D), target validity (V), witnessability (W), or any historical verdict.

scope.in: Changes to an option's semantics (declaration, default, type, apply, readOnly, path) that are traceable to an option-dependent branch predicate; changes to a boolean predicate that directly or indirectly consumes option state and controls selection, emission, enabling, rejection or branch choice.
out: Configuration-value assignments config.<path> = ... (U2): separate mode, not Layer A.
Changes to warning or assertion message text, or to data that a condition reads, when the condition expression itself is unchanged.
Shell or external-command tests (including inside derivation strings); their operands are command output, not Nix option state.
Test-only changes (witness only; counts for R, never for E). Test files are not Layer-A consumers.

Import-list registration, package-only changes, and runtime behavior or observability (README non-goals; layer C). Layer A claims only the selection decision, never downstream runtime behavior of the selected element.

categories.E_DIRECT: The changed construct is an option semantic change traceable to a branch predicate in the same module, OR a changed predicate whose changed term reads only options declared in the same module.
categories.E_INDIRECT: The changed construct is an option semantic change traceable only to a predicate in another module, OR a changed predicate whose changed term reads an option declared in another module (declaration_module_governs), OR whose option state reaches the changed term through a let binding or helper function declared in another module (let_binding_rule).
categories.E_AMBIGUOUS: Traceability, predicate role, or EC10 equivalence cannot be decided by the procedure below (search incomplete or unpinned, predicate role P_UNKNOWN with option operands, EC10 level EQ3, or an operand with no named option path). Not counted as E-positive; reported separately.
categories.E_NO: No change in scope: out-of-scope categories above, traceability established absent (T_NONE under absence_evidence), P_DATA_ONLY or not_nix_predicate, or an equivalent rewrite established at EC10 level EQ0-EQ2.

pr_aggregation: PR category = strongest hunk category in the order E_DIRECT > E_INDIRECT > E_AMBIGUOUS > E_NO. A hunk that declares or reads several options takes the strongest option's category. E-positive = E_DIRECT or E_INDIRECT.

source_evidence.rule: Every traceability, absence and equivalence decision is made on a committed tree identified by a full 40-hex SHA that the search resolves to (git rev-parse --verify <sha>^{commit} equals the required SHA). A working tree, a default-branch code-search index, or any search not pinned to the SHA is not evidence for T_NONE and not evidence for EQ1-EQ2 equivalence. A resolution mismatch or any search error is ERROR, never negative evidence.
source_evidence.procedure: work/go-h/exact_tree_search.sh <repo> <sha> <scope> <extended_regex> [exclude] [receiver_regex]. Status MATCH, ZERO_COMPLETE (the only status that can support absence) or ERROR. Uses git grep exit codes: 0 match, 1 no match, other error.

traceability_search.applies_to: Option-semantic changes (EC01-EC05, EC16-EC19). For a predicate change, the consumer check confirms the changed predicate is in a branch construct; the category is set by predicate_rule.
traceability_search.unit: option path P of the changed option (for a removed option: base side; otherwise head side)
traceability_search.step1: Search the changed module file at the relevant side for a branch construct (mkIf, optional, optionals, if-then-else, assert, && or || or ! with a boolean operand, lib.mkMerge condition, or a P_SELECTION function) whose operand reads P. A reference reads P if P appears in the changed expression or in an attribute path extending P (cfg.package.version reads cfg.package), including value arguments such as lib.optionals cond P. Found in the same module file: T_IN.
traceability_search.step2: If not found in step1, search the committed tree at the same side (exact_tree_search.sh) for the reference patterns of P (full path, exact alias, and the owner-key identifier per absence_evidence A3) in nixos/ with branch-construct context. Found in another module, read in a branch context: T_FOREIGN (positive evidence, one exact occurrence suffices). Absence established under absence_evidence A1-A6: T_NONE. Otherwise: T_UNKNOWN.
traceability_search.record: For each traceability decision record: P, side, SHA, procedure name, query regex(es), grep status and match count, each occurrence (file, line, text) with its branch context, and the T_* decision.

absence_evidence.positive_evidence: One exact occurrence at the required SHA, read in its branch context, establishes T_IN or T_FOREIGN when it reads P under predicate_rule. Positive evidence never needs completeness.
conditions_for_T_NONE: A1 pinned and completed: the search resolved to the required full SHA and returned status MATCH or ZERO_COMPLETE (git grep exit 0 or 1, no ERROR). ERROR is never negative evidence. A1 does not require zero raw matches; absence is decided by A3 after A4 classification.
A2 complete scope: scope covers every file under nixos/ at that SHA. Exclusions are only the declaring module file(s) of P, recorded.

A3 owner-key query: K is the owner key of P, the first segment of P below its top-level namespace (gophernicus for services.gophernicus.rootDir; zfs for boot.zfs.enabled). Pattern \bK\b (identifier, not path) must return zero matches outside the declaring module after A4 classification. A leaf-only or container-path-only query (for example \.rootDir\b or services\.K\.) is a diagnostic superset and is never sufficient alone.

A4 non-consumer classes, excluded by scope.out and recorded per match: documentation (*.md, release notes), import-list lines, test files under nixos/tests (witness only), comments. Any unclassified match makes the result T_UNKNOWN.

A5 receiver closure: every receiver that can reach K without naming K as an identifier must have a closed domain (a literal list, a literal set of names, or a closed enum type) whose members do not include K. Such receivers are: whole-namespace bindings (cfg = config.<namespace>); attrNames/attrValues/attrByPath/getAttr and mapAttrs-family iteration applied to config.<namespace> itself (not to a named sub-attrset such as config.<namespace>.<name>); and computed keys config.<namespace>.${x}. Any open-domain receiver (user-supplied, derived from attrNames or unknown) is T_UNKNOWN. A receiver whose domain includes K is a consumer and T_NONE is refused. `with config.<namespace>` and `inherit (config.<namespace>) x` reach K only by naming it, so they are covered by A3 and are not A5 receivers.
A6 K is not a common word: if A3 cannot be cleanly classified because K matches unrelated identifiers, the result is T_UNKNOWN rather than T_NONE.
absence_evidence.result: T_NONE only when A1-A6 all hold, recorded as an absence record. Any failed or unverifiable condition gives T_UNKNOWN. Never convert an incomplete or default-branch search into negative evidence.
forbidden_sources_for_T_NONE: gh search code (default-branch index, no SHA pin, result cap)
searches truncated or with an unrecorded exclusion
absence_record_fields: decision (T_NONE or T_UNKNOWN) and the failing condition if T_UNKNOWN

predicate_rule.changed_term: Only operands and operators the PR adds, removes or modifies count as the changed term. Unchanged operands are recorded as context.
predicate_rule.declaration_module_governs: The module that declares an operand decides the category of the changed term. A changed term that reads an option declared in another module is E_INDIRECT even when its consumer predicate is in the changed file. A changed term that reads only options declared in the changed module is E_DIRECT. Where the changed term mixes both, any foreign operand makes it E_INDIRECT.
predicate_rule.let_binding_rule: A let binding is transparent for tracing: a binding that is a pure expression of named option paths (and static values) carries the option state of those paths. The category is set by declaration_module_governs of the traced paths, not by the binding site. An exact alias (cfg = config.x) is a direct read of x. A binding that is a helper function declared in another module makes the reads through it E_INDIRECT. This resolves the v3.1 tension between indirect_via_bindings and lambda_over_option_attrset: v3.1 could give E_INDIRECT or E_AMBIGUOUS for the same expression.
predicate_rule.not_nix_predicate: A predicate evaluated by a shell or by an external command (including inside a derivation string) is not an option-branch predicate: E_NO, even when its input path is derived from option values. Option state enters only as the iteration domain.
predicate_rule.data_only: A change to a value (list literal, package set, attribute value) that a predicate reads, when the predicate expression itself is unchanged and the option semantics are unchanged: E_NO (changes output or content only). A boolean whose role is P_DATA_ONLY is E_NO.

predicate_taxonomy.question: Does the boolean control whether a source-level element, path, value, definition or branch is selected, emitted, enabled, rejected or taken?

roles.P_GATING: A boolean value is consumed in a position that determines whether a source-level branch, configuration fragment, assertion, warning, selected element or equivalent guarded structure is taken, emitted or included. Consumers are defined operationally in h1c_gating_vs_data (G0).
roles.P_CONTROL: The boolean chooses which of two or more alternative expressions is evaluated: if-then-else in value position, and guard forms where the other branch is taken when the boolean is false.
roles.P_SELECTION: The boolean is the predicate of a function that keeps or drops elements of a list or attribute set (lib.filter, lib.filterAttrs, builtins.filter, lib.partition, lib.findFirst, lib.remove, and any function whose documented role is keeping or dropping elements by a boolean). The list of functions is not closed; role decides.
roles.P_DATA_ONLY: A boolean is only stored as a value, passed on as ordinary data, returned from a transform, serialized, interpolated into text, or passed to an external consumer, with no identified gating consumer (G1).
roles.P_UNKNOWN: A Nix boolean whose role cannot be classified from the source at the stated side. With option operands it is E_AMBIGUOUS.

predicate_taxonomy.rule: A predicate change is E-eligible iff its role is in eligible_roles, its operands read option state, and the mixed-predicate and causal-relevance rules (h1c_mixed_predicate, h1c_causal_relevance) hold for the watched option. The category then follows declaration_module_governs. P_DATA_ONLY predicates are E_NO. A P_UNKNOWN predicate with option operands is E_AMBIGUOUS.

lambda_rule.predicate_lambda: A lambda passed as the predicate argument of a P_SELECTION callee, where the callee is resolved under h1c_callee_resolution, is a predicate. A lambda passed to a transform callee (h1c_higher_order H2) is not a predicate, whatever its body returns. A boolean produced inside any lambda is classified by h1c_gating_vs_data at its own position.
lambda_rule.eligibility: A predicate lambda is eligible iff its boolean result controls selection (P_SELECTION) and its outcome depends on option state directly or indirectly: through a lambda parameter that iterates an option-derived collection (traced under lambda_over_option_attrset and let_binding_rule), or through a free variable that reads option state.
lambda_rule.lambda_over_option_attrset: A predicate whose operand is a lambda parameter iterating an option attrset or list is traced to the iterated option path P (through let bindings where needed), and P is then searched as in traceability_search. If the iterated collection cannot be traced to a named option path, the result is T_UNKNOWN (E_AMBIGUOUS).
lambda_rule.named_predicates: A predicate passed by name (for example builtins.filter f xs) is classified by resolving the binding of f in the same file at the side. If it cannot be resolved there, P_UNKNOWN.
lambda_rule.boundary: A predicate lambda whose boolean depends only on static values (no option state reaches it, directly or through its iterated collection) is E_NO.

ec10_equivalence.applies_to: A predicate expression or option default/type expression rewritten in the PR (EC10). Decides whether an apparent rewrite is E_NO (equivalent) or a semantic change.

levels.EQ0: Textual identity after normalizing location, whitespace and line breaks.
levels.EQ1: Identical AST after dropping formatting, comments and redundant parentheses.
levels.EQ2: Bounded local normalization, all of the following and nothing else: (a) alpha-renaming of lambda parameters and let bindings without capture; (b) attribute-path sugar with identical AST meaning; (c) commensurate path spelling where a same-file let alias binds exactly the option path; (d) pure lexical alias introduction or removal that satisfies the transparency conditions T1-T6 (h1c_let_alias_transparency), proven by exact-SHA def-use; (e) library alias substitution L1 (h1c_library_binding).
levels.EQ3: Any equivalence needing semantic reasoning: global bindings or imports, dynamic attribute names, non-local computation, operand or list reordering, or any normalization not listed under EQ2. EC10_AUTOMATIC is false for EQ3.

forbidden_automatic: adding or removing mkDefault, mkForce or mkOverride priority wrappers
replacing an expression by a literal with the same current value without evaluating the source
any equivalence whose justification needs a binding outside the same expression, except a library alias chain permitted by h1c_library_binding L1
ec10_equivalence.decision: EQ0-EQ2 equivalent: E_NO with the equivalence stated. EQ0-EQ2 not equivalent: treat as EC03, EC04 or EC12. EQ3: E_AMBIGUOUS until a reviewer decides, with the decision recorded with evidence. EQ0-EQ2 checks are automatic (EC10_AUTOMATIC=true); EQ3 is not (EC10_AUTOMATIC=false).
evidence_record: review_requirement (none for EQ0-EQ2; manual for EQ3)

attribute_rule.rule: Helper-generated declarations (mkPackageOption, mkEnableOption, shared option-generating functions) are option declarations for protocol purposes; their arguments define default and type. Traceability applies to them as to hand-written declarations.

classes.name: removed option declaration
classes.rule: traceability_search on the removed path, base side

classes.name: default, type, or predicate expression rewritten
classes.rule: ec10_equivalence. EQ0-EQ2 equivalent: E_NO with equivalence stated. EQ0-EQ2 not equivalent: EC03, EC04 or EC12. EQ3: E_AMBIGUOUS pending review.

classes.name: boolean predicate changed that consumes option state
classes.rule: predicate_taxonomy role must be eligible; then predicate_rule (declaration_module_governs, let_binding_rule, not_nix_predicate) and lambda_rule for predicate lambdas

classes.name: warning or assertion condition changed
classes.rule: If the condition expression changed: predicate_taxonomy (P_GATING for assertion and warning conditions) and predicate_rule. If only message text changed: E_NO.

classes.name: rename or move of an option (mkRenamedOptionModule, mkRemovedOptionModule, explicit relocation)
classes.rule: traceability_search on the old path (base) and new path (head)

classes.name: option declared through a helper (mkPackageOption, mkEnableOption, shared option-generating function)
classes.rule: as EC01-EC05, with attribute_rule for helpers

classes.name: nested or submodule option
classes.rule: as EC01-EC05 at the nested path

classes.name: option declared with a dotted key
classes.rule: as EC01-EC05; key spelling is not a semantic change

classes.name: build-time check or derivation string test over option-derived values
classes.rule: not_nix_predicate: E_NO. A Nix-level boolean predicate in the same hunk is EC12.

classes.name: data change feeding a predicate, predicate expression unchanged, option semantics unchanged
import-list registration of a module file, or a test registration
classes.rule: E_NO by itself. The imported module's own declarations are classified under their own hunks.

amendments: v3.1: declaration_module_governs made explicit; the result_map no longer sets the category of a predicate change.
v3.1: a reference extending an option path reads that option; value arguments count as reads.
v3.1: EC10 covers relocated or refactored predicates with equivalent evaluation.
v3.1: lambda_over_option_attrset added; untraceable iterated collections are E_AMBIGUOUS.
v3.1: aggregation over several options in one hunk; EC22 for import-list and test registration lines.

v4 (GO-H1B.1): absence_evidence replaces unpinned gh search as the only T_NONE source. T_NONE requires SHA-pinned complete scope, owner-key identifier search, classified non-consumer matches, and receiver-domain closure. gh search and leaf-only or container-path-only searches are forbidden as T_NONE sources.
v4 (GO-H1B.2): positive evidence (one exact occurrence) and absence evidence (A1-A6) are separated; incomplete search yields T_UNKNOWN, never T_NONE.
v4 (GO-H1B.4-7): predicate_taxonomy with roles P_GATING, P_CONTROL, P_SELECTION, P_DATA_ONLY, P_UNKNOWN; eligibility depends on role and option dependence. Syntax lists are not used.

v4 (GO-H1B.5-7): lambda_rule. Predicate lambdas passed to P_SELECTION functions are eligible when their boolean controls selection and depends on option state; transform lambdas are not predicates; Layer A claims only the selection decision.
v4 (GO-H1B.8-11): ec10_equivalence levels EQ0-EQ3; EQ0-EQ2 automatic; EQ3 review-required; forbidden automatic normalizations listed; EC10 evidence record defined.
v4: let_binding_rule resolves the v3.1 conflict between indirect_via_bindings and lambda_over_option_attrset.

amendments.change: Adds h1c_* rules: callee resolution, mixed predicates, causal relevance, let alias transparency, let-bound defaults, gating versus data (operational), higher-order calls, library binding (L1 alias chain as EQ2 (e)), exact-source identity, ambiguity policy, GO-I boundary. Replaces the v4 predicate_taxonomy text for P_GATING and P_DATA_ONLY, and the v4 lambda_rule.predicate_lambda text. Amends ec10 forbidden_automatic to permit only the L1 library alias chain. Keeps U1-U4, categories, traceability, absence standard and classes unchanged. A1 wording corrected: v4 required status ZERO_COMPLETE, which made T_NONE impossible when non-consumer matches exist; A3 already decides absence after A4 classification.

known_gaps: Attribute attribution by text heuristics is unreliable for multi-line Nix strings; the parsed structure is authoritative.
Helper-generated declarations (EC17) may be invisible to text search; this affects D, not E.
Named or higher-order predicates whose body is in another file are P_UNKNOWN until read at the exact SHA (h1c_callee_resolution).
Custom higher-order functions are CALLEE_UNKNOWN unless H3 holds.
EQ3 equivalences, including library semantic equivalences, are reviewer-owned; the protocol claims no automatic equivalence beyond EQ0-EQ2 and L1.
Indirect dependencies beyond bounded static tracing are DEPENDENCY_UNBOUNDED and reviewer-owned.

h1c_callee_resolution.purpose: H1C.1. Predicate role depends on the resolved semantic callee of an application head, not on identifier spelling.

callee_classes.FQ_BUILTIN: builtins.<name>, where builtins is not rebound in any enclosing scope of the use.
callee_classes.FQ_LIB: lib.<path>, where lib is the file's module argument (header { lib, ... }: or { lib }:) and is not rebound in an enclosing scope. Resolved at the exact SHA through lib/ (h1c_library_binding).
callee_classes.LOCAL_ALIAS: an identifier whose unique binding in the enclosing scopes is f = <FQ_BUILTIN or FQ_LIB>, with no rebinding of f on the use path.
callee_classes.BARE: an identifier with no static binding in the file, or reachable only through an enclosing with.
callee_classes.DYNAMIC: application head is a computed attribute selection, a function result, or an import result.

rules.R1: FQ_BUILTIN and FQ_LIB resolve mechanically to a semantic callee at the exact SHA.
rules.R2: LOCAL_ALIAS resolves mechanically only if def-use proves a unique binding to an R1-resolved callee and no intervening rebinding on the use path. Otherwise CALLEE_UNKNOWN.
rules.R3: BARE resolves only through a unique static binding visible at the use, with no enclosing with between binding and use. Otherwise CALLEE_UNKNOWN. Matching the identifier text is never a resolution.
rules.R4: DYNAMIC, an unresolved import, or any callee whose resolution needs reasoning beyond these bounded contracts is CALLEE_UNKNOWN.
rules.R5: CALLEE_UNKNOWN makes the predicate role P_UNKNOWN. With option operands the result is E_AMBIGUOUS. It is a reviewer-owned state, not a validator error.

builtin_roles.builtins.filter: P_SELECTION: argument 1 is the predicate; argument 2 is the list.
builtin_roles.builtins.isString, builtins.isInt, built: value tests. When passed as the predicate argument of a resolved P_SELECTION callee they are the predicate; their operand is each element, so eligibility follows the operand, not the spelling of the test.
builtin_roles.other builtins: classified only when used under a resolved role; otherwise P_UNKNOWN.

h1c_callee_resolution.named_predicates: A predicate passed by name is resolved to its binding in the same file at the side SHA (lambda rule). If that binding is not in the file, its definition is read at the same SHA under R1 or R3; otherwise CALLEE_UNKNOWN.

h1c_mixed_predicate.purpose: H1C.2. A predicate with watched and foreign operands is eligible for the watched option; the foreign operand does not disqualify it.
predicate_record_fields: watched_dependencies[]: {option path, dependency_path[] of def-use edges, edge kinds}
dependency_paths[]: union of the edges above

rules.M1: A predicate with an eligible role and at least one proven watched dependency is eligible for the watched option. Foreign dependencies are recorded and do not disqualify it.
rules.M2: A predicate with only foreign dependencies relative to the target is not a valid Layer-A target for that watched option. The target is invalid (target validity), not E_NO.
rules.M3: The record makes no claim that the watched option is the sole cause of the branch outcome. Other operands are recorded, not dismissed.
rules.M4: Category follows declaration_module_governs: a term with any foreign operand is E_INDIRECT, a term reading only in-module options is E_DIRECT.

h1c_causal_relevance.purpose: H1C.3. Mere textual mention of an option is insufficient; the watched option must feed the predicate through a def-use path.
accepted_edges: direct read in the predicate expression
exact alias binding that satisfies h1c_let_alias_transparency
lambda parameter iterating an option-derived collection (lambda rule)
transparent let binding whose value reads the option and is referenced on the path to the predicate
not_causal: textual occurrence in description, example, defaultText, documentation or message text
a binding with no reference on any path to the predicate (dead or unrelated)
an output payload that the predicate does not consume
h1c_causal_relevance.unbounded: If the path cannot be bounded (read through a function body, dynamic key, unresolved helper), the result is DEPENDENCY_UNBOUNDED. A DEPENDENCY_UNBOUNDED edge is never eligible; the outcome is E_AMBIGUOUS when the predicate is otherwise eligible.

h1c_let_alias_transparency.purpose: H1C.4. A pure let alias may be transparent under bounded proof. Not a general rule for let-bound expressions.

conditions.T1: the binding name is lexically unique in the scopes visible at the use
conditions.T2: no shadowing occurs on the path from binding to use
conditions.T3: the RHS is a static attribute path rooted at an option (config.<path>) or at an exact alias already proven transparent, optionally followed by static attribute selections
conditions.T4: the use is directly traceable: the alias name appears where the option value would appear
conditions.T5: no function call, conditional, dynamic attribute key, coercion or transformation intervenes between binding and use
conditions.T6: each link of a chain of aliases is itself proven under T1-T5

h1c_let_alias_transparency.effect: A chain satisfying T1-T6 is EQ2 (d) for the introduction or removal of the alias. Any unproven link is ALIAS_UNPROVEN and the equivalence is EQ3.
h1c_let_alias_transparency.not_transparent: A let binding whose RHS is a function call, a conditional, a computed key, a transformed value or an expression over several options is not an alias and is not transparent.

h1c_let_bound_defaults.purpose: H1C.5. A let binding that feeds an option property is classified by the property it defines.
chain: approved option property (default, type, apply, readOnly, declaration)
option value where a predicate reads the option (only where the target needs a branch relation)

rules.D1: The change is recorded at the option property path it reaches (for example services.x.y.default). The let is not the eligibility reason.
rules.D2: For a shared binding, only the option property paths the binding reaches are relevant. Other consumers are recorded as not relevant, with the reason.
rules.D3: A default or type change is eligible only if the option has a branch relation under U3 (a predicate reads its value, through a proven edge). Without that edge the change is not E-eligible.
rules.D4: If any link cannot be resolved conservatively, the result is E_AMBIGUOUS.

h1c_gating_vs_data.purpose: H1C.6. An operational test for P_GATING versus P_DATA_ONLY.
G0_gating_consumers: (ii) first argument of a resolved conditional-inclusion callee, whose definition at the exact SHA shows that it returns its second argument when the first is true and otherwise an empty value (for example lib.mkIf, lib.optional, lib.optionals, lib.optionalString, lib.optionalAttrs). The contract is read from the definition, not from the name.
(iii) the assertion attribute of an assertion, or the condition of a warning (P_GATING)
(iv) the predicate argument of a resolved P_SELECTION callee (P_SELECTION)
(v) an operand of && or || whose result is itself in one of positions (i)-(iv)
h1c_gating_vs_data.G1_data_only: The boolean only flows into attribute values not consumed by (i)-(v) in the same file, list elements, string interpolation, serialization or formatting calls, the result of a transform lambda, or external text (shell, configuration file, unit file). An attribute value consumed by an external system is data.
h1c_gating_vs_data.G2_unknown: If the consumer of a boolean cannot be identified within bounded analysis, the role is P_UNKNOWN. With option operands the result is E_AMBIGUOUS.
h1c_gating_vs_data.G3_boolean_operators: The result of && or || is not gating by itself. It is gating only when the whole result is in a G0 position.
h1c_gating_vs_data.G4_no_speculation: A boolean does not become P_GATING because some downstream consumer might eventually branch on it. The consumer must be identified.

h1c_higher_order.purpose: H1C.7. Predicate status belongs to the callback's role at the resolved call site.
h1c_higher_order.H1_selection: filter (predicate over elements), filterAttrs (predicate over name and value), partition, findFirst: the callback is a selection predicate.
h1c_higher_order.H2_transform: map, mapAttrs, concatMap, concatMapAttrs, imap0, imap1, foldl: the callback is a transform, not a predicate, whatever its result type. Booleans inside it are classified by h1c_gating_vs_data at their own positions.
h1c_higher_order.H3_custom: A custom higher-order function is recognized mechanically only if its body is resolved (in-file or at the exact SHA) and shows that the callback result selects elements. Otherwise CALLEE_UNKNOWN.
h1c_higher_order.H4_no_whitelist: The table is the set of resolved callees named here, not a general name whitelist. Other callees are resolved under h1c_callee_resolution or left as CALLEE_UNKNOWN.

h1c_library_binding.L1_alias_chain: A library name whose definition at the exact SHA is a chain of inherit or direct attribute-alias bindings (inherit (X) name; or name = X.name;) ending in a builtins member, with at most 4 steps, all in lib/ at one SHA. lib.<name> is equivalent to builtins.<name> by EQ2 (e). Record the SHA and file:line of every step.
h1c_library_binding.L2_non_alias_definition: A library definition that is not an alias (for example a lambda) requires inlining or beta-reduction to match an inline expression. That is EQ3, reviewer-owned, with the definition's SHA recorded.
h1c_library_binding.L3_no_sha: Without SHA evidence there is no equivalence claim. The result is EQ3 unknown.
h1c_library_binding.L4_name_is_not_evidence: A function name or documentation alone is never evidence of equivalence.

h1c_exact_source_identity.purpose: H1C.10. Every decision that depends on a source fact records the SHA of that source.
required_identities: the module file containing the predicate or the change
the header library file used to resolve lib (callee resolution)
each alias target and each library binding step
each option declaration used for watched or foreign dependencies
each predicate definition used by a named predicate
each library definition used by L1 or L2
h1c_exact_source_identity.non_evidence: Working-tree and default-branch evidence is diagnostic only. It cannot establish a historical target's semantics.

h1c_ambiguity_policy.purpose: H1C.11. Conservative fallback when a case needs reasoning beyond the bounded contracts.
h1c_ambiguity_policy.rule: If a case needs reasoning beyond the bounded contracts, do not stretch automatic classification. Use a reviewer-owned state. Ambiguity is a first-class outcome, not a validator failure.
h1c_ambiguity_policy.absence_note: T_NONE is claimed only under the exact-SHA absence standard (absence_evidence A1-A6). Any unmet condition gives T_UNKNOWN.

h1c_go_i_boundary.purpose: H1C.14. Mechanical versus reviewer-owned responsibilities for GO-I.
mechanical: load source from the exact base or head SHA; never from a working tree
parse Nix syntax to an AST for the supported subset
lexical name resolution within the supported bounded subset
resolve transparent let aliases satisfying T1-T6
resolve known fully-qualified selection constructs under R1
trace watched option to predicate dependencies where locally provable, recording the edges
record foreign predicate dependencies separately, with their declaring module
classify P_GATING and P_DATA_ONLY where G0 and G1 are decidable
